summary.title: Domain-driven design - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: Domain-driven design is a software approach that models code on a business domain using bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, and tactical building blocks like entities, value objects, aggregates, and repositories.
keywords: how to model business domain in code
takeaways: DDD matches code structure and language to the business domain, with a shared ubiquitous language between experts and developers.
Large systems are divided into bounded contexts, each with its own model, rather than one unified model.
Tactical building blocks include entities (identity), value objects (immutable, attribute-based), aggregates with a root, repositories, factories, and services.
Context mapping patterns (e.g. Shared Kernel, Anticorruption Layer, Conformist) describe how bounded contexts relate.
CQRS and event sourcing are often combined with DDD, and bounded contexts often map to microservices.
summary.summary: The Wikipedia article introduces domain-driven design, a approach coined by Eric Evans in 2003 that models software around a domain through input from domain experts. It explains core concepts such as ubiquitous language, entities, value objects, aggregates, domain and integration events, and repositories and factories. It then covers context mapping patterns from Evans, and how DDD relates to CQRS, event sourcing, event storming, model-driven engineering, and microservices. The page also notes critics' concerns and a short list of tools, and it is a general overview with a reference list rather than a hands-on tutorial.
